$comment: track = pitch range in semitones over a control's whole value range (0 = not pitched; slider-tick and slider-landmark: the renderer sends each step's position 0..1 as the sound detail, the player shifts the pitch by (pos - 0.5) x track, Darren 2026-10-21). Facet UI sounds, single source for the WASM workbench (Foundations > Sound). Procedural, no samples: one sound = base + variant.defaults + types[].variants[<variant>] (minus 'use'), engine from the variant; rendered with Web Audio (OfflineAudioContext), DC/edge-fade cleaned and loudness-aligned per 'levels'. Copied 1:1 from Facet main (packages/sounds/src/packs.json + synth.ts BASE, tokens.json sound, site docs meanings). Types = what a sound is for; variants = the six packs (keycap default).

pitch.use: pitched step ticks (slider, dial, arc; sounds with track > 0): semitones at the bottom / top of the control range, linear in between (Darren 2026-10-22: the top went too high; was the symmetric +-track/2, i.e. +-6 in keycap)

engines.basic: Oscillators with partials, filtered noise and a feedback echo.
engines.modal: A short noise strike exciting a few damped sine modes (wood, glass or felt body) plus a few ms of early reflections.

variants.name: Keycap
variants.about: Short tactile clicks: filtered-noise bursts with a small tonal body, like a mechanical key or a camera dial. Chimes turn into a dry marimba.

variants.name: Halo
variants.about: Sine tones with bell partials, soft attacks and a little air. Calm and rounded.

variants.name: Arcade
variants.about: Square and pulse waves with stepped arpeggios: a friendly, retro-digital chiptune feel.

variants.name: Graphite
variants.about: Dry and precise: tight low-mid thocks with a crisp, short strike, like a well-made hardware control. Chimes are a dry glass marimba.

variants.name: Crystal
variants.about: Soft crystalline tones on glass-like mode ratios with feather-light strikes. Bright but short and restrained.

variants.name: Felt
variants.about: Warm and rounded: low wooden bodies struck through felt, with muffled strikes. Chimes are a warm marimba.

rules.$comment: How Facet uses sound (Darren 2026-10-22: "there are rules to why we use stuff and when we use stuff"). Sections in reading order; each item one rule. Rendered by the workbench Sound page and, later, the docs site. Per-type when / not lines live on each type; which component plays what = sound_usage.json (generated from the code) + the hand lines in `usage`.

sections.title: Why sound
items: A wall panel is flat glass: no travel, no click. Sound gives a touch its feel. It says the touch landed and what it did.
A sound stands for a meaning, not a component: the same moment sounds the same everywhere, so it is learnt once (tap in place, open deeper, back, on / off, ticks for values, error when not possible).
Character, not noise: short, quiet, a little fun, never over the top and never an alarm. The panel lives in a home and is heard by everyone in the room.

sections.title: When a sound plays
items: To answer a person: a real tap (LVGL CLICKED: finger down and up on the part), a value step crossed under the finger, or a touch on a blocked part.
Two sounds speak for the house instead: notify (a toast arrives) and timer-done (a timer someone set has finished). They are the only sounds nobody touched for.

One action, one sound: the sound of what the tap means (a Card plays open, never tap + open). A part built from another (a List row with a Toggle, a Header with its Back button) plays the inner part's sound, once.
The sound follows the result: toggle-on when the thing is now on, playing or started; toggle-off when it is now off, paused or stopped.

sections.title: When it must not
items: Finger down on a working part is silent: the press look is the feedback. The sound comes with the tap (CLICKED, on release).
No sound for a scroll, a swipe that scrolls, or a finger that slides off the part: LVGL drops CLICKED, and the sound goes with it.

No sound for things nobody touched: Home Assistant updates (a light switched elsewhere, a value arriving), clock ticks, animations, screens building or rebuilding, a screen opening by itself, the Dial's opening sweep, quiet follow-up toasts.
No tick without a step: a value that did not cross a step is silent, and a drag never ticks more often than it has steps.
Sound off means silent: one switch turns every UI sound off (workbench sidebar Sound: Off; on a panel one setting). Reduced motion does not change sound.

sections.title: Blocked and errors
items: A blocked part is never silent: finger down on a disabled or unavailable part emits blocked and plays error at once (fw::st::blocked, every component), once per touch; letting go does nothing.
A blocked Slider or Dial plays error once on press and never ticks; nothing moves.
error is a low, muted knock: it says "not possible" without scolding. A fault nobody touched (a sensor offline) is a toast, so it plays notify, not error.

sections.title: Which sound
items: Pick by meaning: in place = tap; deeper = open; back or away = back; switching = toggle-on / toggle-off; a value = ticks; done or saved = confirm; not possible = error; something new = notify; a timer ends = timer-done.
Choosing one option of many (Radio, Picker row, Segmented, an accent swatch) is a tap: it acts in place, nothing is switched.
Opening a sheet or a screen is open (Card, Tile, More row, a chevron row, the Speaker button); closing it is back (Back button, sheet Close or scrim, a toast dismissed by a tap or swipe).
A new component reuses these meanings; a new sound type is added only for a moment none of them covers, here first.

sections.title: Loudness and levels
items: Every sound is rendered, cleaned (DC removed, edge fades of levels.fadeMs) and loudness-aligned to levels.loudnessDb with peaks capped at levels.peakDb, so a 20 ms click and a one-second chime feel equally loud. Volume is one master level on top.
The sound heard most is the shortest: ticks, then tap. Length grows with rarity: ticks < tap < toggles < open / back < confirm / error / notify < timer-done.

Panels play the same sounds pre-rendered (mono 16-bit PCM at 16 kHz, levels.sampleRates), decoded at boot so a press never waits for storage; a new sound cuts off the one still playing, so sounds never pile up.

sections.title: Packs
items: A pack (variant) voices all ten sounds with one character; the meanings never change between packs. keycap is the default; a panel plays one pack (the workbench sends the pick with Show on device).

Every pack keeps the same contrasts: open rises and back is its falling mirror; toggle-on is brighter and higher than toggle-off; error is low and muted; timer-done is a friendly phrase, never an alarm; in the modal packs the chimes (confirm, timer-done, notify) share one key.
Procedural, no samples: one sound = base + the pack defaults + the type's values for that pack, in this one file. Change a number here and it changes everywhere.

sections.title: Step ticks and pitch
items: Every step a Slider, Dial or arc crosses counts (steps = range / step). One shared limiter in the core (fw::step_ticks) decides which are heard.
Audible ticks are at least Motion tick-min apart (40 ms, about 25 a second): a slow, dimmer-like drag ticks on every step, a fast drag thins to a steady patter.
Landmark steps (the ends: 0 and 100 %) play slider-landmark, a little stronger and lower, so you feel where the range stops. The limiter never drops one; it waits out the interval.

Pitch follows the value: linear from pitch.low semitones at the bottom to pitch.high at the top (default -6 / +3). The top sits closer to the middle because high ticks turn shrill. Preview other ranges by ear on the workbench Sound page (play-only); the token itself changes only by a code edit Darren asks for.
Ticks come only from the shown value moving under a finger (a drag, or a tap on the track or ring). A value set from elsewhere moves silently.

types.name: Tap
types.for: A plain button press. The quietest, shortest sound, because it is the one you hear most.
types.when: A plain action in place: Button, Icon button (round / square), a List row without a chevron, a Section header action, choosing a Radio, Picker row, Segmented option or accent swatch.
types.not: Not for going deeper or back, switching on / off, or a blocked part. Never on finger down.

halo.use: button press: soft glassy click, ~25 ms

types.name: Open
types.for: Going deeper: a card or row opens its screen. Rising, so it reads as "forward".
types.when: Going deeper: a Card, Tile, More row, a List row with a chevron, the Speaker button (it opens its sheet).
types.not: Not for something opening by itself (a toast, a timer screen), and not for a tap that acts in place.

halo.use: card opens: quick rising two-note blip

graphite.use: card opens: two tight ticks, a fourth up

crystal.use: card opens: rising glass pair, D6 -> A6

felt.use: card opens: two soft knocks, a fourth up

types.name: Back
types.for: Going back: the falling mirror of Open.
types.when: Going back or putting away: the Back button, a Bottom sheet's Close or scrim, a Toast dismissed by a tap or swipe.
types.not: Not when something closes by itself (a toast timing out, a sheet the system closes).

halo.use: back: the falling version of Open

graphite.use: back: the same two ticks falling

crystal.use: back: falling glass pair, A6 -> D6

types.name: Toggle on
types.for: Something switches on or starts. Brighter and a little higher than Toggle off.
types.when: Something is now on, playing or started: Toggle, the Dial's ON / OFF button, Play, a switch row.
types.not: Not for choosing one of many (that is tap), and not when the state changes from elsewhere.

graphite.use: switch on: brighter tick + tiny up-step

crystal.use: switch on: bright glass tick + up-step, E6 -> F#6

types.name: Toggle off
types.for: Something switches off or pauses. Duller and lower, so you can tell the two apart.
types.when: Something is now off, paused or stopped: the same parts as Toggle on.
types.not: Not for closing or going back (that is back), and not when the state changes from elsewhere.

graphite.use: switch off: lower, softer tick + down-step

crystal.use: switch off: softer, lower, C#6 -> B5

types.name: Slider tick
types.for: One detent while dragging. Its pitch follows the value, so a sweep rises or falls.
types.when: A Slider or Dial value crossing a step under the finger (drag, or a tap on the track or ring), through fw::step_ticks: speed-limited by tick-min, pitch from sound.json pitch.
types.not: No tick when the value moves by itself (a Home Assistant update, the Dial's opening sweep), when no step was crossed, or on a blocked control (error once instead). Never more ticks than steps.

keycap.use: detent tick (camera dial); pitch follows the value

halo.use: detent tick while dragging; pitch follows the value

arcade.use: detent tick; pitch follows the value

graphite.use: detent click, quality rotary encoder; pitch follows the value

crystal.use: tiny crystal detent; pitch follows the value

felt.use: soft wooden detent; pitch follows the value

types.name: Slider landmark
types.for: The tick at a landmark step (the ends of the range: 0 and 100 %): the same detent, a little stronger and lower, so you feel where the range stops.
types.when: In place of slider-tick at a landmark step (the ends, 0 and 100 %) while dragging; never dropped by the limiter.
types.not: Not on release and not when the value is set from elsewhere.

keycap.use: landmark tick: detent tick (camera dial); pitch follows the value

halo.use: landmark tick: detent tick while dragging; pitch follows the value

arcade.use: landmark tick: detent tick; pitch follows the value

graphite.use: landmark tick: detent click, quality rotary encoder; pitch follows the value

crystal.use: landmark tick: tiny crystal detent; pitch follows the value

felt.use: landmark tick: soft wooden detent; pitch follows the value

types.name: Confirm
types.for: Done or saved: a short, positive two-note chime.
types.when: Done or saved: a finished action the person waited for (a setting saved, a scene stored, a step completed). No component plays it yet.
types.not: Not for an ordinary tap (tap) or a switch (toggle-on).

graphite.use: done / saved: dry two-note glass-marimba, A5 -> D6

crystal.use: done / saved: two glass bells, A5 -> D6

felt.use: done / saved: warm marimba pair, A5 -> D6

types.name: Timer done
types.for: A timer has finished. A friendly phrase, longer than the rest, but never an alarm.
types.when: A timer someone set has finished. The one long sound; plays once.
types.not: Never repeating like an alarm, never for anything ambient.

halo.use: timer finished: friendly melodic chime, not an alarm

graphite.use: timer finished: short rising pentatonic phrase, D5 F#5 A5 D6

crystal.use: timer finished: A5 D6 F#6 A6, soft glass phrase

felt.use: timer finished: marimba phrase D5 F#5 A5 D6

types.name: Error
types.for: Not possible: a low, muted knock. Never harsh.
types.when: Not possible: finger down on a disabled or unavailable part (fw::st::blocked, every component), once per touch.
types.not: Not for faults nobody touched (those are toasts: notify). Never harsh, never repeated while the finger stays down.

graphite.use: not possible: two low, muted damped knocks

crystal.use: not possible: two muted low glass knocks

felt.use: not possible: two low, felted knocks

types.name: Notify
types.for: Something new needs a glance: a calm ping.
types.when: Something new needs a glance: a toast arrives (Toast layer; layout.json toast.sound).
types.not: Not for quiet follow-up toasts, not for every change in the house, one per arrival.

arcade.use: something new: two-tone ping with echo

graphite.use: something new: calm two-note ping, F#5 -> B5

crystal.use: something new: F#6 -> B5 glass ping

felt.use: something new: warm F#5 -> B5 marimba ping

usage.$comment: Hand-written: when each component plays its sounds (one line per component id). The ids and sounds themselves are generated from the code by tools/gen_sound_usage.mjs (tokens/sound_usage.json), which warns when a line is missing or has no component behind it.
usage.button: Tap: tap. Disabled: error on finger down.
usage.icon_button: Play: toggle-on when it starts playing, toggle-off when it pauses. Round / square: tap. Back role: back. Disabled / unavailable: error.
usage.back_button: The Icon button in its back role: back. Disabled: error.
usage.header: Through its Back button: back; through the Screen chrome's settings button: open.
usage.toggle: Tap: toggle-on / toggle-off by the new state. Disabled / unavailable: error.
usage.slider: Drag or a tap on the track: step ticks (slider-tick, slider-landmark at the ends, pitched by the value). Disabled / unavailable: error once on press.
usage.dial: Drag or a ring tap: step ticks (silent during the opening sweep). ON / OFF button: toggle-on / toggle-off. Disabled / unavailable: error once on press.
usage.list_row: Chevron row: open. Plain row: tap. Toggle row: the Toggle's sounds. Disabled / unavailable: error.
usage.picker_row: Through its List row: tap when an option is chosen. Disabled / unavailable: error.
usage.section_header: Action: tap. Blocked action: error. Title, badge and meta are silent.
usage.segmented: Choosing an option: tap. Disabled: error.
usage.accent_swatches: Choosing a swatch: tap. Disabled: error.
usage.speaker_button: Tap: open (it opens the speaker sheet). Unavailable: error.
usage.bottom_sheet: Close button or a scrim tap: back. Its rows play their own sounds.
usage.toast: Dismissed by a tap or swipe: back. Timing out is silent. Its action Button plays tap.
usage.toast_layer: A toast arrives: notify (quiet follow-ups make none).
usage.layout: Layout foundation demo: the chime toggle plays toggle-on / toggle-off.
